lines.text: Full Page Markdown Report
This fixture is intentionally ordinary markdown. It exists to compare PDF and DOCX pagination
when the author has not supplied layout directives.
Executive Summary
Mote should make a readable document from headings, paragraphs, lists, blockquotes, rules,
and tables. The visual result does not need identical line breaks across PDF and W ord, but the
structure, spacing, and relative proportions should feel close.
The first page contains enough body copy to exercise wrapping. The second page starts
naturally when the content flows beyond the available page height.
A blockquote should be visually distinct, but it should not dominate the page. It is
ordinary document content, not a callout box.
Findings
1. Markdown is the default authoring surface.
2. Directives add semantic document structure only when needed.
3. Tables should use their natural content width unless the author asks for a wider layout.
4. Lists should keep consistent indentation across output formats.
Operating Notes
The following paragraphs are repeated on purpose. They give us a full page without relying on
PDF-specific directives or artificial page breaks.
Progressive authoring means a user can start with a plain markdown memo, add a default font
later, then add a header, footer, section, or table style only when the document needs it. The
backend should preserve that path. A PDF output is visual and final, but it should still reflect the
same neutral document model used by the editable W ord backend.
The paragraph spacing should be comfortable but not airy. Headings should be visibly stronger
than body text. A horizontal rule should span the available text area and separate sections
without looking like a row of typed characters.
